clue.text: Italian lady's apprehensive about French wine

indicators.note: about means the wary word goes around the Italian lady, one wrapped round the other

parts.note: chary means cautious or apprehensive
donna is the Italian for a lady

explanation.surface: An Italian woman is nervous about some wine from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads like 'concerning', but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a white wine grape and wine strongly associated with Burgundy in France.

clue.text: Palm tree taking care of company

parts.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: A palm tree is being looked after by a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The coco is the coconut palm, a tropical tree bearing coconuts.

clue.text: A container filled with mostly luscious fruit

indicators.note: filled with says the vessel holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a pot is a container

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: rich food is luscious and indulgent

explanation.surface: A jar is packed with fruit that is nearly all lush and sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'luscious' sits by 'fruit' as if describing it, but it belongs to the wordplay; only 'fruit' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Trainmen stood off the rails in protest

indicators.note: off the rails means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Railway workers stood around outside the tracks during a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off the rails' rearranges the letters of TRAINMEN STOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration is a public march or rally staged to protest.

clue.text: Steal the Spanish coin

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Pocket the Spanish money.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickel is the American five-cent coin.

clue.text: Tyrant caught traitor following car

indicators.note: following means the later pieces come after the car word

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a rat is someone who betrays others

explanation.surface: A despot nabs a turncoat who was trailing a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocrat rules with absolute power, like a tyrant.

clue.text: Cheap servant's filling niche

indicators.note: filling means the letters sit inside the run of the words cheap and servant's

explanation.surface: A low-paid domestic worker fills an alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Cheap' and the start of 'servant's'.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a recess, often semicircular, at the end of a church, so a kind of niche.

clue.text: Leading US rock band in support

indicators.note: in says the band sits inside the support word

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch
R.E.M. was an American rock band from Georgia

explanation.surface: A top American rock group appears in a backing role.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier as an adjective means foremost or first in rank.

clue.text: Preacher converting evil agents

indicators.note: converting means changing the form of the words, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A minister is bringing wicked spies round to the faith.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelist is someone who preaches the gospel, often travelling to win converts.

clue.text: Pot of cream I whipped up cold

indicators.note: whipped up suggests beating cream into a new form, so its letters with I are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A jug of cream I whisked while it was chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whipped up' rearranges CREAM and I to make CERAMI.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceramic is an item of pottery, so a pot is one.

clue.text: Indian company possesses very strong electronic material that's light

indicators.note: possesses means the company holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: Tata is a large Indian business group
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud or strong
E is short for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: An Indian firm owns a powerful electronic fabric that weighs little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very strong' is the musical marking fortissimo, printed as two letters f.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, fine woven fabric, usually silk, used for lightweight dresses.

clue.text: They hold office party on house

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a function is a formal party or social event
Aries is one of the twelve houses of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Office workers hold a party at someone's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Functionaries are officials, people holding posts in an organisation.

clue.text: Prisoner going down with superior attitude

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
descending means going down

explanation.surface: A haughty convict is being sent down.
explanation.definitionFit: Being condescending means patronising others, acting as if better than them.

clue.text: Cutter in East Anglian waters given signal

parts.note: the Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in Norfolk and Suffolk, in East Anglia
to give the word is to give the signal to act

explanation.surface: A boat on the Norfolk lakes receives a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' looks like a sailing boat, which fits the waters, but it is a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsword is a heavy sword with a wide blade for slashing.

clue.text: Turn corrupt, mostly concealing ace

indicators.note: concealing means the shortened word hides the ace inside it
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: rotten means corrupt or dishonest
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: Go bad, largely by hiding a top card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ROTTEN to ROTTE, and 'concealing' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn about an axis.

clue.text: Like care provided by teacher beyond examination

parts.note: past means beyond, as in going past a point
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A teacher looks after pupils beyond the exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Schools speak of pastoral care, a tutor's attention to pupils' welfare rather than academic work.

clue.text: Woolly dress kit a Wren sports

indicators.note: sports here means displays or shows off, signalling the letters are reworn in a new order

explanation.surface: A Wren, a woman sailor, wears her woollen outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wren is a member of the former Women's Royal Naval Service. 'sports' rearranges KIT A WREN.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitwear is knitted clothing such as jumpers, often woollen.

clue.text: Familiarise Bill with whimsical charm

parts.note: ac, short for account, is a bill
quaint means attractively odd or old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Introduce Bill to someone of quirky appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquaint someone with something is to make them familiar with it.

clue.text: Groomed like Elvis, but I will be ousted by a drunk

indicators.note: ousted by means the named letter is pushed out and the next takes its place

parts.note: Elvis Presley wore a quiff, so his hair was quiffed

explanation.surface: Someone with an Elvis hairdo is thrown out by a drunkard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be ousted by' swaps the I in QUIFFED for A. 'drunk' looks like a noun for a drunkard, but it is the past tense of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaffed means drank heartily, so it is drunk in the past-participle sense.

clue.text: Slough provides men in service

indicators.note: in places the men inside the service word

parts.note: Mass is a church service
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: The Berkshire town Slough supplies soldiers for church.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is also a town west of London, which the surface uses; here it means a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a swamp or bog, as is a slough.

clue.text: Mean hail storm

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, a hail
to rage is to storm angrily

explanation.surface: A cruel hailstorm.
explanation.definitionFit: The average of a set is its arithmetic mean.

clue.text: Guard ate up remainder

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: fed means ate, as animals feed
an end is a leftover piece, a remnant

explanation.surface: A sentry finished off the leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: To defend is to protect or keep watch over.

clue.text: Insult that's set out to stifle panache

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the letters are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A snub meant to dampen someone's flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges STIFLE PANACHE; 'that's' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap in the face is an idiom for a rebuff or affront.

clue.text: Let rip

definitions.meaning: to let a flat is to hire it out for payment
a tear or split in fabric

explanation.definitionFit: Rent is both the act of leasing a property and a tear in cloth.

clue.text: Crime committed by handler of stolen goods

parts.note: by in the sense of authorship, as in a work of someone, gives of
a fence is a dealer in stolen property

explanation.surface: An illegal act carried out by a receiver of loot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'committed' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of the law.

clue.text: Move abroad spurning grand Arab state

indicators.note: spurning means rejecting, so the letter is removed

parts.note: to emigrate is to settle in another country
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Settle overseas while snubbing a great Arab country.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a territory ruled by an emir, as in the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: Legendary queen was idle apparently

definitions.meaning: the queen of Carthage in Virgil's Aeneid
split as did plus a zero, it reads as did nothing, which is being idle

explanation.surface: A mythical ruler who seems to have been lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido founded Carthage in legend; read as did O it means did nothing.

clue.text: It's lustrous but terribly indiscreet

indicators.note: terribly means badly done, signalling the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something shiny that is yet very tactless.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridescent describes a shimmering sheen of shifting colours, a lustrous surface.
